sources.title: As blockbuster game releases run scared from GTA 6, meet the brave devs tackling Rockstar's behemoth head-on
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 . It's got cool cars, crime, a big new city to explore, and the potential to hoover up so much player time that many developers have chosen to give it the widest berth possible. It's led to an October uncommonly packed with big-hitters, and a November - ordinarily one of gaming's biggest months - that's near-barren. But not every developer is steering clear. Despite the potential risks, a select few have looked at GTA 6 and seen not a threat but an opportunity, so what's driving these brave souls? Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School, a first-person puzzle adventure with a popular predecessor, was originally set to launch this September, but like many games this year saw its release date moved. However, its developer bucked the industry trend, shifting its sequel not away from GTA 6's orbit, but closer. "The thing that scares me more than this monocultural event - GTA 6 - is releasing in a week when there are like 15 good games rather than one big one", Coin Crew Games co-founder Wyatt Bushnell tells me when I ask about the studio's decision. Escape Academy 2's original release date might have kept it away from Grand Theft Auto 6, but it would have instead faced a potential "bloodbath" of competition from the likes of Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Blood of the Dawnwalker, Control Resonant, and more. "That was our rationale," Bushnell says. "We can still cut into the GTA stuff, but it would have been a lot harder in September and October." It helps, notes Bushnell, that Escape Academy 2 and Grand Theft Auto 6 - one a contemplative puzzle game, the other a blockbuster action spectacle - are serving very different crowds. That's a sentiment echoed by David Lowey, Atari's senior director of sales and marketing. Atari has similarly bucked industry trends and is releasing two games - Godzilla Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered and Barbie Rewind - in the now largely vacant November window. When we speak, Lowey says there's a clear logic to smaller companies "sneaking" into spots that bigger-budget games can't risk filling, especially if their games differ greatly from Grand Theft Auto 6. "Look at Barbie Rewind coming out on the 12th," he elaborates. "It's a retro game, so it'll pull in people who grew up with these games [and] there's the cosy dreamhouse design at the core ... which is a vastly different game type to GTA 6 and plenty of other games. "It's not an FPS, not a high-octane action game, there's not a lot of combat," Lowey continues. "It's designed to be the exact opposite. It's a game you're meant to curl up in a chair and play." And while he acknowledges the "reality of modern gaming" means there'll be some audience overlap between Barbie Rewind and GTA 6 players - "These sort of older ideas of what people play by gender and age have been smashed", he says - it "won't be the biggest overlap in the world". That, then, makes going toe-to-toe an easier bet. But for Bushnell and Escape Academy, there's another consideration making GTA 6's launch window feel less of a risk: longer-tail sales. "The traditional thinking is that you have this big release and make all of your money in those first two weeks," he explains. "I don't think that holds a tonne of water anymore. The vast majority of sales for Escape Academy were made well after its release. The reality is with digital distribution, discounting, and the fact there is this shelf of games, we're in a world where games last far longer than their initial launch." That means it's less of a concern if GTA 6 sucks up everyone's attention for a few weeks. And for Atari's David Lowey, Godzilla Destroy All Monsters and Barbie Rewind's proximity to GTA 6 has brought added benefits, enabling both games to capitalise on the hype around Rockstar's open-world epic in their own way. "One of the most rewarding things has been the fascination we've seen online around the proximity of Godzilla, Barbie, and GTA," he says. The community has found it easy to root for games releasing in the behemoth shadow of GTA 6. Godzilla Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered - an updated version of the 2002 GameCube party fighting game, which released on 3rd November - has been dubbed, tongue in cheek, the " GTA killer " by fans, while others have joked that Rockstar is " running scared " from Barbie Rewind. "There's no question that this buzz based on the closeness has created player interest," adds Lowey. "In retrospect the timing worked well for us." There's one game, though, that isn't just orbiting GTA 6, it's facing the triple-A juggernaut head-on. Edmund McMillen, Tyler Glaiel, and publisher Nicalis are bringing The Binding of Isaac : Repentance+ to Xbox Series X/S, PlayStation 5, and Switch 2 on 19th November, the same day GTA 6 arrives. "That was [Nicalis'] idea," McMillen laughs when we speak. "'Wouldn't it be funny if...?' I was like, whatever, that's funny ... We're done, so we've got to release this month ... It's a fun experiment." "There's a possibility [Repentance+'s release date] wasn't that stupid an idea," McMillen adds, "and if it was a stupid idea, it's a funny stupid idea." He also hints there's a "funny stupid" thing awaiting players who do a Repentance+ daily run on any platform during GTA 6's launch... McMillen is, though, all too aware of the impact major releases can have on other games. "My heart says it doesn't matter, but my brain has shown me it does," he explains. "When Mewgenics came out it blew up; we went past two million sales almost right off the bat. It was such a blasting, skyrocketing thing for like three weeks. Then Slay the Spire 2 came out, and it sucked everybody out. The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over ... When a new thing comes out, people all move to the new thing ... You can see numbers go from astronomical to very small, and then if the game is good, it'll trickle back in." sources.title: GTA 6's Completely Unrealistic Mountains Had to Be in the Game, Rockstar Says
sources.text: GTA 6 takes some liberties with its world around Vice City If you’ve ever spent time in and around Miami, Grand Theft Auto 6 is bound to delight you. Rockstar Games spared no expense in bringing the diverse world of Florida to life in digital form. Walk down the street in Vice City, and you’re sure to find an approximation of a bar you’ve actually been to . Head to the Leonida Keys, and you’ll find rows of houses on stilts. The attention to detail is impressive, but it also makes one odd detail about the map a little odd. Go all the way north in Leonida, right up to Lummox County, and you’ll be able to go hiking and hunting in the mountains. As any Floridian will tell you, that’s not exactly reflective of the real Florida’s topography. Why take such a major creative liberty there when so much else about Leonida is grounded in realism? In an interview with Polygon, Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson explained why GTA 6 takes players to the mountains. Nelson said that one of the biggest challenges the team faced when designing the game was figuring out the map. Rockstar’s map team began working on the game in 2015, Nelson said, well before anyone else at the studio. While creating another city was easy enough for a team that has mastered that art, expanding to surrounding Florida locales was a tougher proposition. That’s because Florida is a very flat state. The problem with depicting it as is, though, is that GTA players likely would have some expectations about what should be in a modern GTA map. GTA 5 , for instance, built off of Los Angeles to create Los Santos. Because of that, the map has a lot of variety in elevation. That wouldn’t be possible if Leonida stuck too close to reality, so Rockstar ultimately decided to include some mountains to keep GTA 6 a little more consistent with GTA 5 . Though it may not be accurate, it’s a welcome addition to the map. As fun as it is to drive around Vice City, weaving around the same highways can get old. Lummox County offers a lot more open space for off-roading, biking, and other activities that just wouldn’t be possible in a city. For instance, when I found a bicycle perched atop a hill, I found myself racing down a natural BMX course that was built into the world. Every time I head up to Lummox County, it feels like I’m on vacation. Crucially, it’s also the best date spot in the entire game. You can take Jason and Lucia out on impromptu dates throughout GTA 6 , letting the couple play some mini-golf together or blow off steam at a shooting range. One of my favorite play sessions so far simply happened when I got the two in a truck and took them up north to a part of the map I’d never seen. We got out when we found a hiking trail and wound up stumbling into some ruins high up on a hill. It was a peaceful moment of discovery that the two got to share together. Moments like that are what make GTA 6 special, and Leonida’s intricate design is the thing that powers it all.

sources.title: How Long Does It Take To Beat GTA 6?
sources.text: If you couldn't guess by its 210 GB file size, Grand Theft Auto 6 is gigantic. Rockstar's latest open-world game is stuffed to the brim with things to do and steal. It also sports the beefiest story of any GTA game to date. Jason and Lucia star in a sprawling crime epic that takes the couple all around the state of Leonida. While it's difficult to put a consistent hour count on a true 100% playthrough of GTA 6 , we do know that you won't be able to binge it all in one long weekend. Here's how long it takes to beat GTA 6 's story depending on how much side-content you intend to complete. Even if we're just talking about how long it will take you to beat the story and reach the end credits, expect to spend a lot of time with GTA 6 . In our fastest playthrough, we were able to complete the game in around 53 hours . While that playthrough was focused on clearing the story, it still included a healthy number of side-quests, optional robberies, mini-golf games, and plenty of free-form exploration. A faster playthrough may be possible, but note that GTA 6 features several points where players will either have to amass a certain amount of money or wait for a call to proceed to the next story mission. Even if you only plan on playing for the story, you'll likely still need to do some side-activities to get through it all with enough money to reach the final missions. Players who want to take their time can expect an even longer experience. In another playthrough that was more focused on completing lots of optional side-activities, our save file crossed the 100-hour mark. That matches what Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson recently told Polygon about his most recent full-story playthrough before launch, which he said took him just over 100 hours , in a run that he described as "rushed." Though that’s a wide range of hours, what we’ve seen so far in testing lines up with How Long To Beat's data on Red Dead Redemption 2 . User playtime data puts an average main story playthrough at around 52 hours and one with a focus on side-content at 89 hours, which matches with what we found in GTA 6 . All in all, expect to spend 70 to 80 hours clearing the main story unless you plan to mainline it. That makes GTA 6 the series' longest game by a wide margin, so budget your time accordingly.

sources.text: What do you need to fix in Jason’s House? Find out here Wondering how to completely fix Jason’s house in GTA 6? This guide explains all the different odd jobs you need to complete in order to totally fix Jason’s house. You’ll get this objective as soon as you return to his house after the game’s second mission, but you won’t have forever to complete it. Jason’s friend Cal mentions that if Lucia’s going to live at Jason’s house, he better fix the place up. In this guide, we’ll explain all the things you have to fix around the house, and what happens if you don’t do it. For dozens of GTA 6 guides,Â check out our GTA 6 Guide Hub.Â Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. There are four projects to complete around Jason’s house. You can repair these as soon as you get complete control of Jason following the Gone Fishing mission. You won’t be able to complete the projects at Jason’s House after Lucia is free from prison. You’ll be warned to complete these jobs before she returns, but if you miss that, you’re out of luck. You’ll have to fix the steps outside Jason’s house to progress the game, so you can’t miss this. There’s a stack of wood to the side of the stairs. Stand next to them and you’ll be able to repair the steps and enter Jason’s house. To fix the leaky roof in GTA 6, head outside Jason’s house and find the set of ladders that are stacked next to the door. Climb them, walk across the roof to the tarp, and you can repair the leaky roof. To fix the wall in Jason’s House, head into his bedroom, and look for the massive sheets of wood that are leaning up against the wall. This section isn’t just about repairing the wall, you’ll also have to paint the wall. You can chose which colour paint you want to use, but this won’t impact how Lucia reacts to your house, and how much it improves your relationship. The railing can be found next to Jason’s workout equipment. You’ll notice it if you walk out on the back deck, that there are massive gaps in the railing. Head down to the workout equipment, and face the house, and you’ll get the prompt to fix this part of Jason’s House. If you don’t fix Jason’s house, your initial relationship meter with Lucia when she returns from jail will be significantly lower. This is a quick way to make sure that Jason and Lucia get off on a strong foot, and it takes very little time to do. That’s our complete guide to fixing Jason’s house in GTA 6.
